sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: a story page's window shows the page's own picture (the E Street Radio and DJ-set banners) with its title; the Storyteller badge is left out.

Brucebase: a song's window keeps the links of the song's intro under its title (the writers, the original artist, the album); the hover card still shows it as words. Its Lyrics section keeps the "Visit SpringsteenLyrics.com for other versions of this song." link after each version.
Link previews on the Springsteen sites: a link to the page you are on that only adds an #anchor (a jump within the page) no longer opens a preview of that same page.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: links to a song's tour page, its On The Tracks page and its lyrics page now preview (Ctrl+hover), under the song preview's setting. The tour page's card says how often the song was played on tour and on how many tours, the window lists every tour; On The Tracks shows the versions under each song with the releases each is on; a lyrics page's card shows its first four lines and how many versions it has, the window each version (the first open) and the springsteenlyrics.com link last.

Brucebase: links to an album's studio sessions page and to a discography page now preview, under the event, venue, people and release setting. A sessions window has the overview, the credits and each table folded with its first 100 rows; a discography window has the releases under the page's own headings, each with its cover, year, release date and label, and the covers as its pictures. The other stats pages still have no preview.
Brucebase: links to /multi: and /soundcheck: pages preview the show they lead to, as /onstage: links do.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the window of a person or band starts with the biography (About) and its source, and the hover card shows its first sentence.

Brucebase: the window of a release or playlist also shows, folded, its On The Tracks versions under each song (with the releases each is on), its Recording 'Live' Dates under each disc with each date linked to its show, its Gallery/News press links, how often its songs were played live, its notes and history, and the links to its lyrics and media.
Brucebase: a release's page (Release button) shows its Gallery/News press links too, folded above the details.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the window of a show, recording session or interview now starts with the page's description (About this show), and its hover card shows the description's first sentence. A page whose description is plain text above the tabs shows it too, in the page's own view as well.

Brucebase: the window lists the people under the tab's own name: In studio for a recording session (with the session's name first), On set, On site. An interview's playlist is listed like a setlist, each song with its original artist. The venue's other lists (Appearances, Cancelled, Performances without Bruce, the From My Home To Yours episodes) are folded sections, and an older page's News tab shows as News/Memorabilia.
Brucebase: the year table's On stage column shows a recording session's people too.

Brucebase: the window, the year table and the event page's own view now list a show's guests too (a second list on the wiki's page: Bruce Springsteen as guest at another act's show, a radio show's guest after its hosts), and the people of the rarer tabs (On Phone, On Call, In Room). In the year table a line-up with several groups shows each group's members under it.
Brucebase: a window no longer shows the code of the wiki's Flickr gallery as text.

Brucebase: a new WARNING, "Brucebase event page with an 'Onstage' tab": in a year table or year listing, an entry whose page spells its cast tab "Onstage" (one word) is flagged on its Content cell once ▶ Pages has read it, also when the warning's filter is on while pages arrive. Its own settings switch it and its tint off.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: a page's History section, with ✎ and H, is now in its window on every site, MusicBrainz included, not only on brucebase.wikidot.com. From another site the requests carry none of your cookies.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: the year table and the year listings get four columns from each event's own page: who was on stage (the band's members folded), which tabs have something in them (Recording, Storyteller, Media, …), the pictures by kind, and the scheduled start. They fill in after ▶ Pages in the On stage header: the rows you can see, then each row you scroll to, one page a second; a row whose hover card you opened before fills in at once, with no request. A row that could not be read shows ⟳ to ask again.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: a discography page (…/stats:discography-album, -retail, -single, the specials, -video) gets a button that shows every release it lists in one table: year, title, subtitle, cover, release date (with its day, month and year), label, and the section and tab it is under. A cover shows big on hover and opens in the viewer on a click. Nothing is fetched.

Brucebase: the songs registered at the Library of Congress (…/stats:songs-registered) get a button that shows every title in a table with its song page where the wiki's song list has it (one request), the registration record above.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: a song's tour page (…/stats:hungry-heart-tour) gets a button that shows every tour in one table: how often the song was played, the tour's own number of shows, the share with a bar and the page's note, then the other known shows and the public rehearsals. Nothing is fetched.

Brucebase: an album's studio sessions page (…/stats:born-to-run-studio-sessions, and each of its parts) gets a button that shows its tables, one per section and tab: the released and additional recordings, every take of the version history in one table with its name split into song, version, take and date and the wiki's note on the song as a column, the timeline and the potential album sequences; the album, its release date, label, credits and overview above. Nothing is fetched.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: On The Tracks (on song, On The Tracks and release pages) splits a take's name further: "THE HEIST - V2 - take 14" gets a Take column, "JUNGLELAND - V1 (August 1, 1974)" a Date column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Brucebase: on a stats page's Tables (WIP.17), a table whose every row is bold no longer takes its first row as the column names (a studio session's version tables), and a table of one bold row no longer gives its row as the column names to the tables after it.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: the statistics pages (…/stats:…: bootlegs by label, shows with circulating audio, the venues of a state, awards, song counts per tour, performance counts per city, …) get a button for each kind of content they have. List: the page's links in one table with the tab they are under, a show's or venue's title split into date, venue, city, state and country, the wiki's sort forms ("Left Foot (The)", "Band, The") turned round. Tables: the page's own tables, one per tab or heading, the first open, with a Section column where a row names the rows below it. Nothing is fetched; the wiki's page stays below, folded.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: A test of the built-in hidden-columns rows offered on upgrade expected one row; since the Discogs Section rows there are three, so it now re-offers only the one it checks.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: a story page (…/story:…: a show's Storyteller words, an interview, a podcast, a speech, a DJ set) gets a button that shows its words as tables — each moment of the show with the song it leads into, or each speaker's turn, a table per part — with the kind, the date, the show's own page (found with one small request) and who compiled it above.
Brucebase: a story link's window names the page's kind, date, how many moments or turns it has and who compiled it.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: the tag cloud (https://brucebase.wikidot.com/system:page-tags) gets a button that shows every tag in a table: its family (songs and people told apart with the song list and Relations), its weight on the cloud and about how many pages carry it.

Brucebase: a tag's page (…/system:page-tags/tag/storyteller) gets two buttons: the tagged pages as a table (kind, and for a show its date, venue, city, state and country), and the same pages read from the wiki's page lists with when each was created and last changed, its size, comments and tags.
Brucebase: Pages & Tags (…/manage:pages-and-tags) gets three buttons: this page, every page of its list, and every page of the wiki with its tags; the tags one row each.

Brucebase: every link to a tag's page (the cloud, our tables, the tags line under each page, a window's Tags) shows how many pages carry the tag and the newest six on hover; Space opens the tag's pages in the window, the first 250 at once and "Load all" for the rest.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase Recent changes: each row's page has a ✎ button that opens the page's History in the window on that revision against the one before it (an older revision too: the list's later pages are read for it).
Brucebase History: every comparison scrolls to its first changed line and marks it; and on the wiki's own History (signed in), a comparison opened there scrolls to its first difference.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase: the year listing pages (https://brucebase.wikidot.com/2026-list, …, /1949-64-list) get two buttons. Events turns the year's list into a table — Event (linked to the show on the year page, with its card and window), Date with its parts, Venue, City, State, Country, Note (Recording Session, Rehearsal, Rescheduled, …) and Tour (from the Start of / End of boxes); All years reads every year's listing into one table. Under the year pages' switch.
Brucebase: a tour box that ends one leg and starts the next in one line ("End of the 1st leg, and Start of the 2nd leg of …") now starts the new leg, on the year pages too.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the window of a show on its year page (e.g. an event's "Info & Setlist") shows the year page's icons — Photo, Setlist, Memorabilia, Video, Bootleg, … — each with its name, instead of a line of words.

Brucebase: every Brucebase window (a venue, a person, a show, a song; on Brucebase or from another site) opens any link in the same window, as a MusicBrainz window does: a venue's "Source: Wikipedia" shows the article there, with Back.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: links to a show on its year page (an event's "Info & Setlist", a release's "recorded July 6, 1981", e.g. /2026#020526) now preview on Brucebase's own pages too — the card on hover, the show in the window on Space — as they already did on every other site. Clicking one still goes to the year page.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Brucebase: the wiki's top-bar menus (Manage Site, Help Docs, …) can be used again. Their entries opened under our toolbar and status line, and the menu closed as the pointer moved down onto them, before any button was pressed too. The wiki's header is now lifted over our pinned toolbar, as MusicBrainz's top header already was.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The Brucebase window's History section: chips for the kinds of change (All, Source, Title, Page name, Tags, Metadata, Files, each with its count; several at once) filter the revisions at once; a tag change in the list shows as pills (+ tour_lohadnk, − album_thepromise); From and To on every row compare any two revisions, the older always on the left and the revisions between them tinted; every comparison shows the tags of both (added +, removed struck, or "the same in both") and a changed page title or page name. The list is read 100 revisions a page, and a revision that changed only tags no longer reads the page's text twice (WIP.8's History section).

"✎ Page history" is now in the ☰ menu of every Brucebase page with the toolbar, Recent changes and the year pages included (their own history: the 2026 page is at revision 310). Links to Brucebase story pages (the Storyteller words of a show) preview them, with the story's words and the History section, so a story page's title changes and renames can be seen too.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Every Brucebase preview window on brucebase.wikidot.com ends with a folded "History" section: the page's revisions, newest first (number, date, who, the kind of change, the comment), and what the revision you click changed — the old lines and the new ones side by side, the changed words marked, the unchanged lines folded ("Everything" shows them), a revision that changed only tags or the title saying so. You need not be signed in: the wiki answers its history to everyone (probed signed in and signed out). Nothing is read until the section opens; then 20 revisions ("Load 20 more" for older ones) and the two texts the change needs, one request a second, kept until you leave the page. ✎ in the window's title bar and H open it; on a page that has a window, the ☰ menu's "✎ Page history" opens it for the page itself. Setting: Page history in the Brucebase window (on).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Help: the window's History section; two places still named the event preview setting by its old label.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase release and playlist pages get a button, "Release": a table per edition and disc (song, running time, where the track comes from, the page's footnote on it; a box set's films each a table of their own), the personnel, the related releases, a live release's recording dates (the show's date and place, linked), the takes On The Tracks and how often each song was played live. Above them the facts the page states (released, label, produced, recorded, mixed, mastered, design, photography), each edition's running time, the overview, footnotes and history, tags, media, the lyrics' pages and the artwork typed by its file names; the wiki's page folded below. Nothing is fetched.

Brucebase bootleg pages get "Bootleg": the tracklist, a table per disc with each song's time and, where the page marks them, the sides; the label, catalog number, time, format, source and sound in a Bootleg card, the notes and the Front, Back and Disc artwork. The wiki writes bootlegs as free text — lists, numbered lines, "Disc 1: (43:31)", "//" after a side's last song — and all of it is read.

Links to Brucebase release, playlist and bootleg pages preview them (Ctrl+hover): their facts and tracks; Space opens the window with the overview, personnel and related releases. The settings are now called "Detail pages: events, songs, venues, people, releases and bootlegs as tables" and "Preview event, venue, people, release and bootleg pages on hover".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A YouTube player embedded as "youtube.com/embed/playlist?list=…" (Brucebase's release pages) was taken for a video named "playlist"; it is the playlist.
Brucebase On The Tracks: a take written "THE HEIST - V2 - take 14" or "JUNGLELAND - V1 (August 1, 1974)" is now split into title and version too (song pages and the new release pages).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the shows in a person's lists link the wiki's "on stage" pages, which the wiki forwards to the show; these links now preview the show itself, card and window.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A new WARNING on the Brucebase detail pages, "Brucebase entry with a comma after its date": an entry the wiki lists as "2015-04-30, Story Chapel, …" instead of "2015-04-30 Story Chapel, …". It is still read; the Date cell is tinted, its tooltip quotes the entry, and the lists being the linked pages' titles, that page's title is the one to fix. Settings "Find Brucebase entries with a comma after their date" and its highlight (both on).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase venue pages get a button, "Venue": the performances, cancelled shows and appearances at the venue as tables, its description, region, count, map link and pictures above, the wiki's page folded below.

Brucebase pages of people and bands get "Person": every performance with Bruce Springsteen as one table — the wiki splits long lists into pages (Steven Van Zandt's 1,517 shows over six), and every page is read, one request each — with an As column saying in which band; the count per band; appearances; the recordings by song and role; their bands or members (in reading order: "The E Street Band"); songs co-written with Bruce. The biography, tags and pictures are above. The setting is now called "Detail pages: events, songs, venues and people as tables".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase song pages get a button, "Song": the credits (each release, who played what), the performances counted by tour (only the tours it was played on, with its share of the shows), every performance, multiple performances on one date, snippets, the official live downloads and its takes On The Tracks (title, take, running time, the bootlegs and releases it is on), as tables you can filter and sort. Above them: where the song comes from, Released on Album, the lyrics and notes (folded), a Song card (how often and when last played live, released on, live downloads, takes), its tags, media and links; the wiki's page folded below. An On The Tracks page gets "Versions": its takes as one table. Nothing is fetched. The setting is now called "Detail pages: events and songs as tables".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase event pages (a gig, a show that did not happen, a recording session, a rehearsal, an interview) get a button, "Event", that lays the page out like a MusicBrainz release, from the page itself with nothing fetched. Above the tables: what it was, where and when; About this show; an Event card (type, date and weekday, scheduled time, venue, tour, the year page, running time), the page's tags by family and its YouTube links; the pictures with a chip per kind and per photographer. The tables: the Setlist as one table (Set, #, Song in MusicBrainz style, Segue, Premiere ★ for a song in bold on the wiki, Note), who was on stage with their band and role, the other shows at the venue (this one in bold), the recordings (official releases, bootlegs with their labels, the live download) and the Storyteller's words by song. The wiki's own page stays below, folded, its headings folding too. Setting "Event pages: a detail view of the gig" (on). Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/3rAGVKsBHEv9jGspkJ5X7Z

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Brucebase previews: the scheduled time is read on pages that write it "Scheduled: 21:00 | Local Start Time …" too; the card left it out.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase previews: a picture now says what its file name tells, the photographer included ("Photo · Cliff Breining · #01", "Setlist · #01a · Handwritten", "Pass · #01 · Backstage"), in the window and in the full-size viewer. The window shows the photos once per photographer, those without a known photographer last. Each group folds on a click on its heading, and a Ctrl+click folds or opens every group at once, so a gig with hundreds of photos can be folded away; the text sections stay as they are.

Brucebase previews: the window ends with the page's tags, folded at first, sorted into Date, Place, Tour, On the page, Songs, People, Releases and more; each tag links to the wiki's list of pages with it. Previews already cached are read once more.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the side bar's show/hide handle now sits at the top of the side bar, as the MusicBrainz sidebar's does, instead of halfway down the window. Scrolled down, it stays near the top of the window; with the side bar hidden, it sits at the top of the page content.
